requirement: For each project source location Habeas supplies, the address MUST consist of the project-relative file and outline selector under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. This applies to the source metadata in mandatory inputs, acknowledgments, site matches and citation reviews, and to locations in Habeas tool diagnostics. These addresses MUST omit line and column coordinates. Quoted source retains its text, and an argument error may quote the agent's input.

structural: `requirements.authoring.no_line_numbers` states only observable output behavior. Each source address Habeas supplies MUST consist of the project-relative file and an outline selector (per `requirements.references.outline_selectors`). This applies to mandatory inputs, acknowledgments, site matches, citation reviews and tool diagnostics. The addresses MUST omit line and column coordinates. Quoted source and echoed agent input are explicitly exempt.

I checked each clause for a structural obligation. None names a library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface.
- "the address MUST consist of the project-relative file and outline selector": a different internal representation would give identical output. Examples are a plain string, a differently shaped struct, or a formatter in another module. That representation would still satisfy the clause, so the choice is discretionary.
- "These addresses MUST omit line and column coordinates": this constrains what appears in output. It does not constrain how the code is built. An implementation that tracks spans internally but never emits them still conforms.

`requirements.references.outline_selectors` is only cited context. Any selector-grammar obligation belongs to that declaration and its refinements, not to this subject.

No implementation roots were supplied. Since no structural obligation needs implementation evidence, no root is missing. Whether the output omits coordinates is a behavioral matter, left to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each observable obligation of `requirements.authoring.no_line_numbers`. The `{test}` markers are present, so there is no marking gap. I did not read any implementation source.

**Mandatory inputs, acknowledgments and the prompts they feed.**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[subjects_of_one_kind_share_a_byte_identical_system_prompt]` builds subjects of every kind: structural, example, citation and site.
- For each subject it checks that every mandatory input and every model acknowledgment has string `file` and `item` fields.
- It also checks that the metadata, with `text` and `body` removed, matches none of the position patterns. Those are `.rs:N`, `line N`, and `line`, `column` or `start_line` keys.
- The rendered system and subject prompts are checked against the same patterns.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` checks the exact JSON for an anchored root-file input. That input has `file`, `item` (empty), `hash`, `kind` and `text`, and no coordinates.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[optional_requirement_and_example_reads_preserve_the_complete_declarations]` checks that optional declaration reads carry no `line`, `line_start` or `line_end` fields.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[behavioral_review_discovers_implementation_locations_without_receiving_their_bodies]` checks that a read returns `file` and `selector` values (`src/lib.rs`, `fn[ready]`).

**Site matches and citation reviews.**
- `src/sites.rs#mod[tests]/fn[sites_are_the_innermost_nodes_of_site_matches_and_violations_within_them]` asserts the exact `matches_value()` JSON. It contains `kind`, `query`, `item` (a selector) and `text`, and no line fields.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[site_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_applies_and_the_site]` checks the site subject message. It uses the file `src/lib.rs` and the selector `fn[check_two]`.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_the_item_and_citations]` checks the citation record `file`, `item` and `citations` payload, and the `<root>` selector.

**Tool diagnostics and discovery output.**
- `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tool_errors_drop_the_source_line_of_a_parse_error]` checks diagnostics with `line N`, `:N:` and `at line N, column M` forms, including a duplicate-declaration message that cites two locations. All are reduced to `file#`.
- The same test checks that a `read_lines` argument error keeps the line numbers the agent supplied. This matches the carve-out for argument errors that quote the agent's input.
- `src/authoring/domain_tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[named_query_errors_identify_the_source_without_exposing_a_line_number]` checks that a named-query error names `md/requirements.md#` with no line number.
- `src/authoring/domain_tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[domain_discovery_returns_readable_nodes_without_recording_their_contents]` checks that lookup and query results carry no coordinate keys. It also checks `source_address` returns selectors.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[outline_tool_rejects_excluded_and_unreadable_sources_without_domain_reads]` checks that outline, read and structural-search payloads match no position pattern. The structural-search hit returns the selector `fn[intact]`, and the read result has `file` and `selector` fields.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[source_tool_results_use_selectors_and_keep_locations_inside_quoted_code]` checks that the read, outline, text-search and structural-search results contain no coordinates outside quoted code. The `src/lib.rs:123` text inside quoted source is preserved. Missing-selector and invalid-selector errors give `quoted.rs#fn[...` with no line numbers.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[explicit_ignored_reads_return_an_error_and_the_assessment_continues]` checks that denied, missing and malformed read errors contain no line numbers.
- `src/github.rs#mod[tests]/fn[the_tool_reads_issues_with_the_token_and_redacts_bodies]` is also marked. It only checks that the GitHub tool output has no position keys, which is a weak check but harmless.

**Result.** The project-relative file plus selector form, the omission of line and column coordinates, the retention of quoted source text, and the allowance for an argument error to quote the agent's input are each exercised with assertions. The assertions would fail if a coordinate leaked into any of these surfaces. I found no unexercised obligation.
